security_audit.summary: Of 115 static findings, four are confirmed: unpinned package execution, insecure token-file creation, and credential forwarding in two HTTP helpers. The remaining alerts reflect documented client behavior, Markdown formatting, or readable multilingual text. A semantic finding covers quota tokens in URLs; no evidence found of malicious intent or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The documented npx command downloads and executes the latest external package without review or a pinned version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version, verify lockfile integrity, and require informed approval before downloading or executing it.

remediation.issue: Quota tokens are saved with default filesystem permissions in a predictable temporary file.
remediation.suggestion: Create the credential directory with mode 0700. Write credentials through exclusive, symlink-safe temporary files with mode 0600, then replace atomically.

remediation.issue: HTTP helpers can forward X-FS-Quota headers across redirects without validating the destination origin.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and validate endpoint origins. Reject cross-origin redirects or strip credentials before following them.

remediation.issue: Quota balance requests place bearer tokens in URL query strings.
remediation.suggestion: Use the X-FS-Quota header for balance and validation requests. Redact tokens from diagnostics and access logs.

remediation.issue: Free-service and semantic-engine claims conflict with the bundled client's token gate and lexical implementation.
remediation.suggestion: Distinguish bundled lexical features from external semantic features. Reconcile token requirements and billing guidance before suggesting payments.

content.user_title: Find Visual Styles from Mood Descriptions
content.value_statement: Everyday mood descriptions often lack precise art-direction vocabulary. This skill matches descriptions to ranked visual styles, definitions, and reference vocabulary through local matching and optional online lookups.
actual_capabilities: Rank visual styles from descriptions of up to 500 characters, returning names, definitions, scores, and matched terms.
Match cached terms locally, recognize explicit style names, and optionally expand matches with synonym glosses.
Use optional cloud analysis when local word matching finds nothing and both permission and a quota token are present.
Query online word relationships and vocabulary associated with a visual style.
Retrieve online style details and reference-image metadata for up to five style identifiers per batch.
Inspect cache and connectivity status, manage quota tokens, and return readable text or structured output.
limitations: The bundled client needs Python 3.8 or later. Offline analysis requires a previously downloaded, usable dictionary cache; expired caches can fail.
Local matching is lexical, not full semantic interpretation; the separately recommended MCP package is outside this reviewed bundle.
Online features depend on service availability and changing billing policy. Cloud fallback requires permission and a token, despite documentation describing free access.
The skill does not generate images or guarantee reference-image licensing; placeholder images are not valid style samples.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use feeling-search offline for this mood: [description under 500 characters]. Return three candidate styles, definitions, and matched words. Report a missing cache without networking.

prompt_templates.prompt: Look up [mood word] online and list its associated styles, related words, and opposites. Use endpoints documented as free.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: inspect vocabulary relationships through online lookup.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Reference Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [up to five style identifiers]. Ask before potentially billed requests. Include definitions, image kinds, credits, licenses, and source links. Exclude placeholders.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare style references with provenance.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Style Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [description] locally, then try fuzzy matching if needed. Ask before cloud fallback and confirm possible costs. Return ranked styles, matched terms, source, and limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage fallback, consent, and result provenance.

output_examples.input: Describe styles for the documented Chinese example about walking alone past a convenience store in rain under cold white lighting.
output: Documented local example: the matched terms include light and white.
Documented candidate styles include the Delft School, Ashen Winter, and De Stijl.
These are lexical candidates, not a definitive interpretation of the scene.

output_examples.input: Analyze a mood offline before a dictionary cache has been downloaded.
output_examples.output: No local dictionary cache is available. Download the dictionary while online, then retry offline. No network request was made.

best_practices: Use short, concrete descriptions and review matched words before accepting a style ranking.
Download the dictionary with approval, verify cache freshness, and use offline mode when descriptions must stay local.
Confirm online costs, protect quota credentials, and preserve image credits and licensing information.
anti_patterns: Treating a local lexical match as full semantic understanding or the only correct artistic direction.
Enabling cloud analysis, spending quota, or executing the external MCP installer without informed approval.
Using placeholder images as authentic examples or assuming all references permit commercial reuse.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code are supported. The bundled client requires Python 3.8 or later and uses standard-library modules.

faq.question: Does the skill generate images?
faq.answer: No. It returns style candidates, vocabulary, and online reference-image metadata that can inform a separate image-generation workflow.

faq.question: Can I work entirely offline?
faq.answer: Local analysis needs a previously downloaded, usable dictionary cache. Expired caches can fail offline; word relationships and image lookups require network access.

faq.question: Is cloud analysis free?
faq.answer: Documentation describes free service, but billing can resume. The bundled client still requires explicit permission and a quota token for cloud fallback.

faq.question: Does the bundled client understand negation and semantic meaning?
faq.answer: Local analysis uses term matching and optional synonym glosses. Semantic-engine and negation claims refer to an external MCP package or service.

faq.question: What data can leave my machine?
faq.answer: Cloud analysis sends your description and quota token. Other online commands send lookup terms, style identifiers, credentials, or supplied claim information.
